subject: Literature
title: Harriet Beecher Stowe and Uncle Tom's Cabin
description: One-minute skill: Harriet Beecher Stowe and Uncle Tom's Cabin.

hook.text: Lincoln reportedly told Stowe, 'So you're the little woman who wrote the book that started this great war.'

buildup.text: Uncle Tom's Cabin sold three hundred thousand copies in its first year and made the horrors of slavery viscerally real.

discovery.text: Stowe translated abolitionist arguments from political abstraction into emotional stories that ordinary readers could feel.

twist.text: Southern states banned the book. Some made it a crime to own a copy, proving how much they feared its power.

climax.text: Stowe proved that a novel by a woman could shift national politics and accelerate the march toward war and freedom.

punchline.text: One woman's novel helped start the war that ended slavery.

quiz.question: How did Southern states react to Uncle Tom's Cabin?
options: They praised it as a fair depiction of plantation life
They banned it and made it a crime to own a copy
They ignored it as irrelevant fiction
